es.L: Y estaban en el camino subiendo a Jerusalén, y Jesús iba delante de ellos, y se asombraban, y los que seguían tenían miedo.
es.B: Iban por el camino, subiendo a Jerusalén, y Jesús caminaba delante de ellos. Los discípulos estaban asombrados, y los demás que iban detrás tenían miedo.
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos iban por el camino que sube a Jerusalén. Jesús caminaba delante de ellos. Los discípulos estaban asombrados por esto. Los demás que iban detrás tenían miedo.

sw.L: Nao walikuwa njiani wakipanda kwenda Yerusalemu, na Yesu alikuwa akitangulia mbele yao, nao walikuwa wakishangaa, na wale waliokuwa wakifuata waliogopa.
sw.B: Walikuwa njiani wakipanda kwenda Yerusalemu, na Yesu alikuwa akitangulia mbele yao. Wanafunzi walishangaa, na wengine waliofuata waliogopa.
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa njiani wakipanda kwenda Yerusalemu. Yesu alikuwa akitembea mbele yao. Wanafunzi walishangaa kwa jambo hilo. Watu wengine waliokuwa wakifuata waliogopa.

decisions.choice: going up to Jerusalem: Jerusalem stands high in the hills
decisions.reason: Travelers always went up to Jerusalem, which lies high in the hills of Judea. Pilgrims coming to the Passover took the road from Jericho (10:46).

decisions.choice: they were astonished, those who followed were afraid: perhaps two groups
alternatives: one group, the disciples, both amazed and afraid
decisions.reason: Mark may mean the disciples were amazed while others in the crowd following were afraid. He may also be describing the same people in two ways.

decisions.choice: Jesus was going ahead of them: he leads the way to his suffering
alternatives: he was walking alone by chance
decisions.reason: Jesus walks in front, knowing what waits in Jerusalem (8:31; 9:31). His resolve amazes and frightens those behind him.

decisions.choice: The disciples ... the others who followed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the two groups as Mark seems to mean them. This follows the more likely reading.

source.text: καὶ παραλαβὼν πάλιν τοὺς δώδεκα ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς λέγειν τὰ μέλλοντα αὐτῷ συμβαίνειν ὅτι Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς γραμματεῦσιν, καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν θανάτῳ καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καὶ ἐμπαίξουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐμπτύσουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ μαστιγώσουσιν αὐτὸν καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν, καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken again the twelve he began them to tell the things being about him to happen, \v 33 Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and to the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and will hand over him to the Gentiles, \v 34 and they will mock him and will spit upon him and will flog him and will kill, and after three days he will rise.

en.L: And taking the twelve aside again, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to tell them the things that were about to happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: \v 33 "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death and will hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Gentiles, \v 34 and they will mock {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and flog {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kill [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], and after three days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise."
en.B: Again {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the Twelve with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and began telling them the things that were about to happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 33 "We are on our way up to Jerusalem," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "and there the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, who will condemn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death and hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Gentiles. \v 34 They will make fun of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, whip {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; and three days later {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise."
en.R: Jesus took the Twelve away from the others again. He began to tell them the things that would soon happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 33 He said, "Listen! We are going up to Jerusalem. There the Son of Man will be handed over to the leading priests and the teachers of God's law. They will decide that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must die. Then they will hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Romans, who are not Jews. \v 34 They will laugh at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They will beat {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with whips and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But three days later {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come back to life."

es.L: Y tomando consigo otra vez a los doce, comenzó a decirles las cosas que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} iban a suceder: \v 33 «{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, subimos a Jerusalén, y el Hijo del Hombre será entregado a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a los escribas, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} condenarán a muerte y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregarán a los gentiles, \v 34 y se burlarán de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} escupirán y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} azotarán y [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] matarán, y después de tres días resucitará».
es.B: Otra vez llevó consigo a los Doce y comenzó a decirles lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} iba a suceder. \v 33 «Ahora subimos a Jerusalén —dijo—, y allí el Hijo del Hombre será entregado a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a los escribas. Ellos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} condenarán a muerte y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregarán a los gentiles. \v 34 Se burlarán de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} escupirán, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} azotarán y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} matarán; y a los tres días resucitará».
es.R: Jesús volvió a llevarse aparte a los Doce. Comenzó a contarles lo que pronto {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} iba a pasar. \v 33 Les dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! Vamos subiendo a Jerusalén. Allí el Hijo del Hombre será entregado a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a los maestros de la ley. Ellos decidirán que tiene que morir. Después {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregarán a los romanos, que no son judíos. \v 34 Ellos se burlarán de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} escupirán. Lo azotarán con látigos y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} matarán. Pero tres días después volverá a la vida».

sw.L: Na akiwachukua tena wale kumi na wawili, alianza kuwaambia mambo yatakayompata: \v 33 "Tazama, tunapanda kwenda Yerusalemu, na Mwana wa Adamu atakabidhiwa kwa wakuu wa makuhani na kwa waandishi, nao watamhukumu kifo, na kumkabidhi kwa watu wa mataifa, \v 34 nao watamdhihaki, na kumtemea mate, na kumpiga mijeledi, na kumuua; na baada ya siku tatu atafufuka."
sw.B: Aliwachukua tena wale Kumi na Wawili, akaanza kuwaeleza mambo yatakayompata. \v 33 Akasema, "Sasa tunapanda kwenda Yerusalemu. Huko Mwana wa Adamu atakabidhiwa kwa wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi, nao watamhukumu kifo na kumkabidhi kwa watu wa mataifa. \v 34 Watamdhihaki, watamtemea mate, watampiga mijeledi na kumuua; na siku tatu baadaye atafufuka."
sw.R: Yesu aliwachukua tena wale Kumi na Wawili mbali na watu wengine. Akaanza kuwaambia mambo ambayo yangempata hivi karibuni. \v 33 Akasema, "Sikilizeni! Tunakwenda Yerusalemu. Huko Mwana wa Adamu atakabidhiwa kwa wakuu wa makuhani na walimu wa sheria. Wataamua kwamba ni lazima afe. Kisha watamkabidhi kwa Warumi, ambao si Wayahudi. \v 34 Watamcheka na kumtemea mate. Watampiga kwa mijeledi na kumuua. Lakini siku tatu baadaye atakuwa hai tena."

decisions.choice: the third prediction of the passion: the fullest of the three
decisions.reason: Jesus has foretold his death and rising in 8:31 and 9:31. This time he names Jerusalem, the chief priests and scribes, the Gentiles, and the mocking, spitting and flogging. Each is told in 14:53-15:20.

decisions.choice: handed over: delivered up, first to the Jewish leaders, then by them to the Gentiles
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice: the Son of Man is handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they hand him over to the Gentiles (15:1).

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the Roman governor and his soldiers
decisions.reason: The word means the nations, people who are not Jews. Here it means the Roman rulers, who alone could carry out a death sentence (15:1-20).

decisions.choice: after three days
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "on the third day", the wording of Matthew 20:19 and Luke 18:33. The SBLGNT reads "after three days", as Mark has it in 8:31 and 9:31. Both mean the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: taking aside: taking with him apart from the others
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the Twelve alone, away from those who were following.

decisions.choice: kill: the Greek leaves "him" to be understood
decisions.reason: The object is clear from the verbs before it.

decisions.choice: handed over
decisions.reason: All levels say "handed over", as in 9:31, since the verb is wider than betrayal and is used for both steps here.

decisions.choice: the Romans, who are not Jews; come back to life
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Gentiles were in this case and what rising means.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre; los jefes de los sacerdotes; los escribas (L, B), los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used across the Gospels in the New Testament drafts. "Hijo del Hombre" is Jesus' title for himself, never under the gender setting. Readable says what the scribes were, teachers of the Law, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: los gentiles (L, B); los romanos, que no son judíos (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "the nations", here the Roman governor and his soldiers (meaning decision m3). "Los gentiles" is the usual Spanish for non-Jews; Readable names them, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu; wakuu wa makuhani; waandishi (L, B), walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used across the Gospels in the New Testament drafts. "Mwana wa Adamu" is the settled Swahili title, never under the gender setting. Readable says what the scribes were, teachers of the Law, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: watu wa mataifa (L, B); Warumi, ambao si Wayahudi (R)
decisions.reason: "Mataifa" alone means the nations; "watu wa mataifa" is the usual Swahili for the Gentiles, here the Roman governor and his soldiers (meaning decision m3). Readable names them, as the English Readable does.

source.text: Καὶ προσπορεύονται αὐτῷ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης οἱ υἱοὶ Ζεβεδαίου λέγοντες αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, θέλομεν ἵνα ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσωμέν σε ποιήσῃς ἡμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And come up to him James and John the sons of Zebedee saying to him, Teacher, we desire that whatever we might ask you you would do for us.

en.L: And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, we want {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to do for us whatever we ask {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.B: Then James and John, Zebedee's sons, came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "Teacher," they said, "we would like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to do whatever we ask of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: Then James and John, the two sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus. They said, "Teacher, please do for us whatever we ask."

es.L: Y se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercan Santiago y Juan, los hijos de Zebedeo, diciéndole: «Maestro, queremos que nos hagas lo que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pidamos».
es.B: Entonces Santiago y Juan, los hijos de Zebedeo, se acercaron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. «Maestro —{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron—, queremos que hagas por nosotros lo que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pidamos».
es.R: Entonces Santiago y Juan, los dos hijos de Zebedeo, fueron a ver a Jesús. Le dijeron: «Maestro, por favor, haz por nosotros lo que vamos a pedirte».

sw.L: Na Yakobo na Yohana, wana wa Zebedayo, wanamjia, wakimwambia, "Mwalimu, tunataka utufanyie lolote tutakalokuomba."
sw.B: Kisha Yakobo na Yohana, wana wa Zebedayo, walimjia. Wakasema, "Mwalimu, tungependa utufanyie lolote tutakalokuomba."
sw.R: Kisha Yakobo na Yohana, wana wawili wa Zebedayo, walimjia Yesu. Wakamwambia, "Mwalimu, tafadhali, utufanyie lolote tutakalokuomba."

decisions.choice: come up: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: whatever we ask: an open request for a favor
decisions.reason: Right after Jesus has spoken of his death (10:33-34), the two ask for honor for themselves. The request is like Herod's open promise in 6:22-23.

decisions.choice: James and John: two of the first four called (1:19-20)
alternatives: other men named James and John
decisions.reason: With Peter they saw the raising of Jairus's daughter (5:37) and the transfiguration (9:2). Jesus named them Boanerges, sons of thunder (3:17).

decisions.choice: please do for us whatever we ask
alternatives: we want you to do for us whatever we ask you
decisions.reason: Readable puts the request in a simple form.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί θέλετε ποιήσω ὑμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, What do you desire I should do for you?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "What do you want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"
en.B: "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them.
en.R: Jesus asked them, "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo: «¿Qué {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} haga?».
es.B: «¿Qué {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que haga por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?», les preguntó.
es.R: Jesús les preguntó: «¿Qué {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que haga por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?».

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Mnataka {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niwafanyie nini?"
sw.B: "Mngependa niwafanyie nini?" aliwauliza.
sw.R: Yesu aliwauliza, "Mngependa niwafanyie nini?"

decisions.choice: what do you want me to do for you: the same question Jesus asks Bartimaeus (10:51)
decisions.reason: Mark sets the two answers side by side. The brothers ask for glory; the blind man asks to see.

decisions.choice: want ... I should do: Jesus does not promise until he hears the request
alternatives: he agrees to do whatever they ask
decisions.reason: He asks them to say what they want before he answers.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δὸς ἡμῖν ἵνα εἷς σου ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ εἷς ἐξ ἀριστερῶν καθίσωμεν ἐν τῇ δόξῃ σου.

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, Grant to us that one of you at right and one at left we might sit in the glory of you.

en.L: And they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Grant us that we may sit, one at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right and one at [{{deity_pronoun:your|Your}}] left, in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory."
en.B: They answered, "Grant that when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory, one of us may sit on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right and one on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} left."
en.R: They answered, "When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rule as King in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory, let one of us sit at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right side and the other at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} left side."

es.L: Y ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Concédenos que nos sentemos uno a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} derecha y otro a [{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}] izquierda en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gloria».
es.B: Ellos respondieron: «Concédenos que, cuando {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} estés en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gloria, uno de nosotros se siente a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} derecha y el otro a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} izquierda».
es.R: Ellos contestaron: «Cuando {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} reines como Rey en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gloria, deja que uno de nosotros se siente a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} derecha y el otro a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} izquierda».

sw.L: Nao wakamwambia, "Utujalie tuketi, mmoja upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na mmoja upande wa kushoto [{{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}], katika utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}."
sw.B: Walijibu, "Utujalie kwamba utakapokuwa katika utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, mmoja wetu aketi upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na mwingine upande wa kushoto {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}."
sw.R: Walijibu, "Utakapotawala kama Mfalme katika utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, mmoja wetu na aketi upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na mwingine upande wa kushoto {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}."

decisions.choice: at your right and at your left: the places of highest honor beside a king
decisions.reason: The seat at a king's right hand was the place of greatest honor and power (1 Kings 2:19; Psalm 110:1), and the left the next.

decisions.choice: your glory: the glory of the Son of Man when he comes as king
decisions.reason: Jesus has spoken of the Son of Man coming in the glory of his Father (8:38). The brothers expect him to rule soon.

decisions.choice: the request misunderstands Jesus' path
decisions.reason: They believe Jesus will reign, but they have not grasped that his way to glory is through death (10:33-34). At the cross the places at his right and left are taken by two rebels (15:27).

decisions.choice: When you rule as King in your glory
decisions.reason: Readable says what the brothers expect Jesus' glory to be.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε· δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω, ἢ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθῆναι;

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus said to them, Not you know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, or the baptism that I am baptized to be baptized?

en.L: But Jesus said to them, "You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?"
en.B: Jesus said to them, "You have no idea what you are asking for. Can you drink the cup that I am drinking, or be baptized with the baptism I am going through?"
en.R: Jesus said to them, "You do not understand what you are asking. I must drink a cup of suffering. Can you drink it? I must go through a baptism of suffering. Can you go through it?"

es.L: Pero Jesús les dijo: «No {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} lo que {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}. ¿{{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} beber la copa que yo bebo, o ser bautizados con el bautismo en el que yo soy bautizado?».
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «No {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} idea de lo que {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}. ¿{{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} beber la copa que yo estoy bebiendo, o ser bautizados con el bautismo por el que estoy pasando?».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «No {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}} lo que {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}. Yo tengo que beber una copa de sufrimiento. ¿{{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} beberla {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}? Yo tengo que pasar por un bautismo de sufrimiento. ¿{{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} pasar {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} por él?».

sw.L: Lakini Yesu akawaambia, "Hamjui mnachoomba. Je, mnaweza kunywa kikombe ambacho {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninakunywa, au kubatizwa kwa ubatizo ambao {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninabatizwa?"
sw.B: Yesu aliwaambia, "Hamjui hata mnachoomba. Je, mnaweza kunywa kikombe ninachokunywa, au kubatizwa kwa ubatizo ninaoupitia?"
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia, "Hamwelewi mnachoomba. Ni lazima {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninywe kikombe cha mateso. Je, ninyi mnaweza kukinywa? Ni lazima nipitie ubatizo wa mateso. Je, ninyi mnaweza kuupitia?"

decisions.choice: the cup: the suffering God gives him to bear
alternatives: a cup of wine at a feast
decisions.reason: In the prophets the cup stands for God's judgment, which the wicked must drink (Isaiah 51:17; Jeremiah 25:15; Psalm 75:9). In Gethsemane Jesus prays that this cup may be taken from him (14:36).

decisions.choice: the baptism: being overwhelmed by suffering, as by deep water
alternatives: the rite of baptism in water
decisions.reason: The verb means to be plunged under. The Psalms speak of trouble as floods that cover a person (Psalm 69:2-3; 42:8). Luke 12:50 has a similar saying about Jesus' death.

decisions.choice: drink, am baptized: present tenses, the suffering already begun or certain
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of his suffering as already under way.

decisions.choice: a cup of suffering; a baptism of suffering
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup and the baptism stand for, which the other levels leave as pictures.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δυνάμεθα.

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, We are able.

en.L: And they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We are able."
en.B: "We can," they told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: They said, "Yes, we can."

es.L: Y ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Podemos».
es.B: «Podemos», {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron.
es.R: Ellos dijeron: «Sí, podemos».

sw.L: Nao wakamwambia, "Tunaweza."
sw.B: "Tunaweza," walimwambia.
sw.R: Walisema, "Ndiyo, tunaweza."

decisions.choice: we are able: a confident answer that they do not yet understand
alternatives: they know exactly what he means
decisions.reason: When Jesus is arrested, all the disciples run away (14:50).

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω πίεσθε καὶ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθήσεσθε, τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἢ ἐξ εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν δοῦναι, ἀλλ’ οἷς ἡτοίμασται.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus said to them, The cup that I drink you will drink, and the baptism that I am baptized you will be baptized; \v 40 but to sit at right of me or at left not is mine to give, but for whom it has been prepared.

en.L: And Jesus said to them, "The cup that I drink you will drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized; \v 40 but to sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right or at [{{deity_pronoun:my|My}}] left is not {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} to give, but [it is] for those for whom it has been prepared."
en.B: Jesus told them, "The cup I drink, you will drink, and with the baptism I am going through you too will be baptized. \v 40 But a seat at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right or at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} left is not mine to grant. Those places belong to the ones for whom they have been prepared."
en.R: Then Jesus said to them, "You will drink from the same cup of suffering as I do. You will go through the same baptism of suffering. \v 40 But I am not the one who chooses who will sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right side or at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} left side. God has prepared those places for the people he has chosen."

es.L: Y Jesús les dijo: «La copa que yo bebo, la {{plural_you:beberán|beberéis}}, y con el bautismo en el que yo soy bautizado {{plural_you:serán bautizados|seréis bautizados}}; \v 40 pero el sentarse a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} derecha o a [{{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}}] izquierda no es {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}} concederlo, sino [que es] para quienes ha sido preparado».
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «La copa que yo bebo, la {{plural_you:beberán|beberéis}}, y con el bautismo por el que yo paso también {{plural_you:serán bautizados|seréis bautizados}}. \v 40 Pero sentarse a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} derecha o a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} izquierda no es cosa mía concederlo. Esos lugares son para aquellos para quienes han sido preparados».
es.R: Entonces Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes beberán|Vosotros beberéis}} de la misma copa de sufrimiento que yo. {{plural_you:Pasarán|Pasaréis}} por el mismo bautismo de sufrimiento. \v 40 Pero no soy yo quien decide quién se sentará a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} derecha o a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} izquierda. Dios ha preparado esos lugares para las personas que ha elegido».

sw.L: Naye Yesu akawaambia, "Kikombe ambacho {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninakunywa mtakinywa, na ubatizo ambao {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninabatizwa mtabatizwa; \v 40 lakini kuketi upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} au upande wa kushoto [{{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}] si {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} kutoa, bali [ni] kwa wale ambao imeandaliwa kwa ajili yao."
sw.B: Yesu aliwaambia, "Kikombe ninachokunywa mtakinywa, na ubatizo ninaoupitia mtabatizwa nao. \v 40 Lakini kuketi upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} au wa kushoto {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} si juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kukitoa. Nafasi hizo ni za wale ambao zimeandaliwa kwa ajili yao."
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliwaambia, "Ninyi mtakunywa katika kikombe kile kile cha mateso ninachokunywa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Mtapitia ubatizo ule ule wa mateso. \v 40 Lakini si {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninayechagua nani ataketi upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} au upande wa kushoto {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Mungu ameandaa nafasi hizo kwa ajili ya watu aliowachagua."

decisions.choice: you will drink, you will be baptized: they will share his suffering
decisions.reason: Jesus promises them suffering, not seats of honor. Acts 12:2 tells that Herod Agrippa put James to death with the sword.

decisions.choice: has been prepared: a passive, God is the one who prepared it
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed, a common way of speaking of God's action. Matthew 20:23 says "by my Father".

decisions.choice: at my right or left: perhaps pointing ahead to the cross
decisions.reason: In 15:27 two rebels are crucified with Jesus, one on his right and one on his left. Mark may want readers to see the irony.

decisions.choice: God has prepared those places for the people he has chosen
alternatives: for whom it has been prepared
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who prepares, as the passive implies.

decisions.choice: cosa mía, with no deity_pronoun span (B)
decisions.reason: The span follows the English: Literal marks "mine" ({{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}), while the English Balanced leaves "mine" plain here, so the Spanish Balanced does too.

source.text: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἤρξαντο ἀγανακτεῖν περὶ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωάννου.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard the ten began to be indignant about James and John.

en.L: And when the ten heard [it], they began to be indignant about James and John.
en.B: When the other ten heard about this, they became angry with James and John.
en.R: The other ten followers heard about this. They were angry with James and John.

es.L: Y al oír[lo], los diez comenzaron a indignarse contra Santiago y Juan.
es.B: Cuando los otros diez se enteraron, se enojaron con Santiago y Juan.
es.R: Los otros diez discípulos se enteraron de esto. Y se enojaron con Santiago y Juan.

sw.L: Na wale kumi waliposikia, walianza kuwakasirikia Yakobo na Yohana.
sw.B: Wale kumi wengine waliposikia jambo hilo, waliwakasirikia Yakobo na Yohana.
sw.R: Wale wanafunzi wengine kumi walisikia habari hiyo. Wakawakasirikia Yakobo na Yohana.

decisions.choice: be indignant: angry at what they felt was wrong
decisions.reason: The same word is used of Jesus in 10:14.

decisions.choice: the ten were angry: they wanted the same honor
decisions.reason: Their anger shows they too were thinking of rank, as in 9:34. Jesus speaks to all twelve in 10:42-45.

decisions.choice: the other ten
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the ten are the rest of the Twelve.

source.text: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ δοκοῦντες ἄρχειν τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι αὐτῶν κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And having called near them Jesus says to them, You know that those being accounted to rule the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and the great ones of them exercise authority over them.

en.L: And calling them to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], Jesus says to them, "You know that those who are considered rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
en.B: Jesus called them to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and told them, "You know that those who are thought of as rulers of the nations lord it over their people, and their important men use their power over them.
en.R: Jesus called them all together and said, "You know how it is with the people who rule over the nations. They like to show that they are the masters. Their leaders use their power to control people.

es.L: Y llamándolos a [{{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}}], Jesús les dice: «{{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que los que son tenidos por gobernantes de los gentiles se enseñorean de ellos, y sus grandes ejercen autoridad sobre ellos.
es.B: Jesús los llamó junto a {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que los que son considerados gobernantes de las naciones dominan a sus pueblos como amos, y sus hombres importantes les imponen su poder.
es.R: Jesús los llamó a todos y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}} cómo son los que gobiernan las naciones. Les gusta mostrar que son los amos. Sus jefes usan su poder para dominar a la gente.

sw.L: Na Yesu, akiwaita [{{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}], anawaambia, "Mnajua kwamba wale wanaodhaniwa kuwa watawala wa watu wa mataifa huwatawala kama mabwana, na wakuu wao hutumia mamlaka juu yao.
sw.B: Yesu aliwaita {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, akawaambia, "Mnajua kwamba wale wanaohesabiwa kuwa watawala wa mataifa huwatawala watu wao kama mabwana, na wakuu wao hutumia mamlaka yao juu yao.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaita wote pamoja, akawaambia, "Mnajua jinsi walivyo wale wanaotawala mataifa. Wanapenda kuonyesha kwamba wao ni mabwana. Viongozi wao hutumia nguvu zao kuwadhibiti watu.

decisions.choice: considered: those who are thought to rule, or recognized as rulers
alternatives: those who only pretend to rule
decisions.reason: The word can simply mean recognized. It may also hint that their rule is only apparent, since God is the true ruler.

decisions.choice: lord it over, exercise authority over: rule harshly, using power for themselves
decisions.reason: Both verbs are strengthened forms that suggest power used against those under it.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the nations of the world and their rulers
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the way kings and governors of the nations rule, as Rome ruled at that time.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: They like to show that they are the masters
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

decisions.choice: se enseñorean de ellos ... ejercen autoridad sobre ellos
decisions.reason: The two Greek verbs are compounds that mean ruling over others harshly, for one's own sake (meaning decision m2). "Enseñorearse" keeps the picture of acting as lord, as the English Literal "lord it over" does.

source.text: οὐχ οὕτως δέ ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν· ἀλλ’ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ μέγας γενέσθαι ἐν ὑμῖν, ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος, καὶ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι πρῶτος, ἔσται πάντων δοῦλος·

records.literal_gloss: Not thus however it is among you; but whoever desires great to become among you will be your servant, \v 44 and whoever desires among you to be first will be of all slave.

en.L: But it is not so among you; but whoever wants to become great among you will be your servant, \v 44 and whoever wants to be first among you will be slave of all.
en.B: That is not how it is among you. Instead, whoever among you wants to become great must be your servant, \v 44 and whoever among you wants to be first must serve everyone as a slave.
en.R: But it is not like that with you. If you want to be great, you must serve the others. \v 44 If you want to be first, you must be a slave to everyone.

es.L: Pero no es así entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; al contrario, el que quiera llegar a ser grande entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} será {{plural_you:servidor de ustedes|vuestro servidor}}, \v 44 y el que quiera ser primero entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} será esclavo de todos.
es.B: Entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no es así. Al contrario, el que entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} quiera llegar a ser grande tiene que ser {{plural_you:servidor de ustedes|vuestro servidor}}, \v 44 y el que entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} quiera ser el primero tiene que servir a todos como esclavo.
es.R: Pero entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no es así. Si alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} quiere ser grande, tiene que servir a los demás. \v 44 Si alguno quiere ser el primero, tiene que ser esclavo de todos.

sw.L: Lakini kwenu sivyo; bali yeyote atakayetaka kuwa mkuu kati yenu atakuwa mhudumu wenu, \v 44 na yeyote atakayetaka kuwa wa kwanza kati yenu atakuwa mtumwa wa watu wote.
sw.B: Kwenu sivyo ilivyo. Badala yake, yeyote kati yenu anayetaka kuwa mkuu ni lazima awe mhudumu wenu, \v 44 na yeyote kati yenu anayetaka kuwa wa kwanza ni lazima awatumikie wote kama mtumwa.
sw.R: Lakini kwenu si hivyo. Mtu yeyote kati yenu akitaka kuwa mkuu, ni lazima awahudumie wengine. \v 44 Mtu yeyote akitaka kuwa wa kwanza, ni lazima awe mtumwa wa wote.

decisions.choice: it is not so: a present, the way things are among Jesus' followers
decisions.reason: Jesus states what is true of his community. Some manuscripts have the future "it shall not be", which makes it a command.

decisions.choice: servant: one who waits on others
decisions.reason: The word is the one in 9:35. It is used of those who serve at table.

decisions.choice: slave: one owned by another, with no rights of his own
decisions.reason: The word is stronger than servant. A slave belonged to a master and had no standing. Jesus asks those who would be first to take the lowest place of all.

decisions.choice: will be: a future that works as a command
decisions.reason: As in 9:35, the future states what must be.

decisions.choice: must be
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the force of command.

decisions.choice: If you want to be great
alternatives: whoever wants to become great among you
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the hearers directly, as in 9:35.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where the word for slave stands against the word for servant in one saying: the step down from servant to slave is the point (m3).

decisions.choice: servidor for the servant; esclavo at every level for the slave
decisions.reason: The servant is one who waits on others (meaning decision m2). The slave is owned by another and has no rights of his own (meaning decision m3), and the saying turns on that, so "esclavo" is kept at every level, as the English keeps "slave" (English decision r-en-3), rather than the softer "siervo".

decisions.choice: mhudumu for the servant; mtumwa at every level for the slave
decisions.reason: The servant is one who waits on others (meaning decision m2), which "kuhudumia" says. The slave is owned by another and has no rights of his own (meaning decision m3), and the saying turns on that, so "mtumwa" is kept at every level, as the English keeps "slave" (English decision r-en-3), rather than the softer "mtumishi".

decisions.choice: Mtu yeyote kati yenu akitaka ...
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "If you want" (English decision r-en-2). A plural "mkitaka" would make the whole group the subject; "mtu yeyote kati yenu" keeps the Greek's one person at a time.

source.text: καὶ γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Even for the Son of Man not came to be served but to serve and to give the life of him a ransom for many.

en.L: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life [as] a ransom for many."
en.B: The Son of Man {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} came, not so that others would serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but to serve them and to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life as the ransom price for many."
en.R: The Son of Man {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} did not come so that people would serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He came to serve others. He came to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life as a ransom, the price paid to set many people free."

es.L: Porque también el Hijo del Hombre no vino a ser servido, sino a servir y a dar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida [como] rescate a cambio de muchos».
es.B: Porque el Hijo del Hombre mismo no vino para que otros {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} sirvieran, sino para servirlos y para dar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida como precio de rescate por muchos».
es.R: El Hijo del Hombre mismo no vino para que la gente {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} sirviera. Vino a servir a los demás. Vino a dar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida como rescate, el precio que se paga para dejar libres a muchas personas».

sw.L: Kwa maana hata Mwana wa Adamu hakuja kuhudumiwa, bali kuhudumu, na kutoa uhai {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} [uwe] fidia badala ya wengi."
sw.B: Kwa kuwa Mwana wa Adamu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} hakuja ili wengine wamhudumie, bali kuwahudumia, na kutoa uhai {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kuwa gharama ya fidia kwa ajili ya wengi."
sw.R: Mwana wa Adamu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} hakuja ili watu wamtumikie. Alikuja kuwatumikia wengine. Alikuja kutoa uhai {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kuwa fidia, yaani gharama inayolipwa ili watu wengi wawe huru."

decisions.choice: ransom: the price paid to set a slave or prisoner free
alternatives: a fee paid to the devil
decisions.reason: The word was used of money paid to free a slave or captive (Leviticus 25:51-52) and of a payment that saved a life that was forfeit (Exodus 21:30; 30:12). Jesus gives his own life as that price. Mark does not say to whom it is paid.

decisions.choice: for: in place of, instead of
decisions.reason: The preposition commonly means in exchange for, or in place of. His life is given in place of theirs.

decisions.choice: many: a great number, set against the one who gives his life
decisions.reason: In Hebrew thought "many" can mean the great multitude, with no thought of leaving others out. The contrast is between the one and the many, as in Isaiah 53:11-12 and Romans 5:15-19.

decisions.choice: to give his life a ransom for many: the suffering servant of Isaiah 53
decisions.reason: Isaiah 53:10-12 says the servant's life is made an offering for sin, that he pours out his life to death and bears the sin of many. Jesus speaks of himself as that servant.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man came to serve: a reversal of Daniel 7:14
decisions.reason: In Daniel 7:13-14 the one like a son of man is given a kingdom, and all peoples serve him. Jesus says the Son of Man came first to serve.

decisions.choice: life: his whole self, his life given up in death
alternatives: his soul as distinct from his body
decisions.reason: The word can mean soul or self; here, as in 8:35, it means a person's life.

decisions.choice: the ransom price
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "price" so that the meaning of ransom is clear.

decisions.choice: a ransom, the price paid to set many people free
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a ransom is in a short added phrase.

decisions.choice: a cambio de muchos (L); por muchos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The preposition means "in place of" (meaning decision m2); "a cambio de" keeps the exchange that a ransom is, as in Matthew 20:28. Balanced and Readable use the plainer "por".

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre mismo, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English "himself" takes the setting. In Spanish "mismo" here is an adjective agreeing with "el Hijo del Hombre", not a pronoun, so it stays plain.

decisions.choice: uhai
decisions.reason: The Greek word can mean soul or life; here it is his whole self, his life given up in death (meaning decision m6). "Uhai" is life itself, as in Matthew 20:28; "nafsi" would suggest the soul.

decisions.choice: badala ya wengi (L); kwa ajili ya wengi (B)
decisions.reason: The preposition means "in place of" (meaning decision m2), which "badala ya" says exactly. Balanced uses the plainer "kwa ajili ya".

source.text: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἰεριχώ.

records.literal_gloss: And they come to Jericho.

en.L: And they come to Jericho.
en.B: Then they came to Jericho.
en.R: Then Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers came to the city of Jericho.

es.L: Y llegan a Jericó.
es.B: Luego llegaron a Jericó.
es.R: Después Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos llegaron a la ciudad de Jericó.

sw.L: Nao wanafika Yeriko.
sw.B: Kisha walifika Yeriko.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walifika katika mji wa Yeriko.

decisions.choice: Jericho: an old city near the Jordan, about fifteen miles from Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jericho lies in the Jordan valley, far below Jerusalem. Pilgrims from Galilee and Perea passed through it on the steep road up to the city.

decisions.choice: come: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers; the city of
decisions.reason: Readable names who came and says what Jericho was.

source.text: καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ Ἰεριχὼ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλου ἱκανοῦ ὁ υἱὸς Τιμαίου Βαρτιμαῖος τυφλὸς προσαίτης ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν.

records.literal_gloss: And as was going out he from Jericho and the disciples of him and a crowd large, the son of Timaeus Bartimaeus, blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.

en.L: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going out from Jericho with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and a large crowd, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going out of Jericho with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and a large crowd, Bartimaeus son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.
en.R: As Jesus was leaving the city with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers and a big crowd, a blind man was sitting beside the road. He was begging. His name was Bartimaeus, which means son of Timaeus.

es.L: Y al salir {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} de Jericó con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y una multitud considerable, el hijo de Timeo, Bartimeo, un mendigo ciego, estaba sentado junto al camino.
es.B: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} salía de Jericó con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y una gran multitud, Bartimeo, hijo de Timeo, un mendigo ciego, estaba sentado junto al camino.
es.R: Cuando Jesús salía de la ciudad con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y mucha gente, un hombre ciego estaba sentado al lado del camino. Estaba pidiendo limosna. Se llamaba Bartimeo, que quiere decir hijo de Timeo.

sw.L: Na alipokuwa akitoka Yeriko pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na umati mkubwa, mwana wa Timayo, Bartimayo, kipofu mwombaji, alikuwa ameketi kando ya njia.
sw.B: Alipokuwa akitoka Yeriko pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na umati mkubwa wa watu, Bartimayo mwana wa Timayo, kipofu mwombaji, alikuwa ameketi kando ya njia.
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa akitoka mjini pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na umati mkubwa wa watu, kipofu mmoja alikuwa ameketi kando ya njia. Alikuwa akiomba msaada. Jina lake lilikuwa Bartimayo, maana yake mwana wa Timayo.

decisions.choice: the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus: the name means son of Timaeus
decisions.reason: Bar is Aramaic for son, so Mark explains the name. He gives the name perhaps because Bartimaeus was known to the first readers.

decisions.choice: a blind beggar by the road: begging from pilgrims on their way to the Passover
alternatives: a man without a home only
decisions.reason: Blind people often had no other way to live than begging. The road out of Jericho was busy with pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the road: the same word as "the way"
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for Jesus' journey (10:32). At first Bartimaeus sits beside the way; in 10:52 he follows on it.

decisions.choice: which means son of Timaeus
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name in a short sentence.

source.text: καὶ ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζαρηνός ἐστιν ἤρξατο κράζειν καὶ λέγειν· Υἱὲ Δαυὶδ Ἰησοῦ, ἐλέησόν με.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard that Jesus the Nazarene it is, he began to cry out and to say, Son of David Jesus, have mercy on me.

en.L: And when he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say, "Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!"
en.B: When he heard it was Jesus of Nazareth, he started to shout, "Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!"
en.R: Bartimaeus heard that Jesus from Nazareth was passing by. So he began to shout, "Jesus, Son of David, show mercy to me!"

es.L: Y al oír que era Jesús el nazareno, comenzó a gritar y a decir: «¡Hijo de David, Jesús, ten piedad de mí!».
es.B: Cuando oyó que era Jesús de Nazaret, se puso a gritar: «¡Hijo de David, Jesús, ten piedad de mí!».
es.R: Bartimeo oyó que pasaba Jesús de Nazaret. Entonces comenzó a gritar: «¡Jesús, Hijo de David, ten compasión de mí!».

sw.L: Naye aliposikia kwamba ni Yesu Mnazareti, alianza kupaza sauti na kusema, "Mwana wa Daudi, Yesu, nihurumie!"
sw.B: Aliposikia kwamba ni Yesu wa Nazareti, alianza kupiga kelele, "Mwana wa Daudi, Yesu, nihurumie!"
sw.R: Bartimayo alisikia kwamba Yesu wa Nazareti alikuwa akipita. Basi akaanza kupiga kelele, "Yesu, Mwana wa Daudi, nionee huruma!"

decisions.choice: Son of David: the King God promised from David's family
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose kingdom would last forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16). By this time "Son of David" was a name for the Messiah. Only here in Mark is Jesus called by it, as he goes up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: have mercy on me: show me kindness and help me
decisions.reason: The cry asks for pity and help, as people cried to God in the Psalms (Psalm 6:3).

decisions.choice: the Nazarene: the man from Nazareth
decisions.reason: The word names Jesus by his home town, as in 1:24.

decisions.choice: Jesus of Nazareth (B); Jesus from Nazareth (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the name comes from.

decisions.choice: ten piedad de mí (L, B); ten compasión de mí (R)
decisions.reason: A cry for help from someone able to give it (meaning decision m2). "Ten piedad" is the plain, living form of that plea, as in Matthew 20:30; Readable uses the everyday "compasión". The same in verse 48.

decisions.choice: nihurumie (L, B); nionee huruma (R)
decisions.reason: The blind man asks for pity that acts to help him (meaning decision m2). "Kuhurumia" is the everyday word for that and suits a cry from the roadside, as in Matthew 20:30; Readable uses the plainer "kuonea huruma". The same in verse 48.

source.text: καὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ πολλοὶ ἵνα σιωπήσῃ· ὁ δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν· Υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.

records.literal_gloss: And were rebuking him many that he should be silent; but he much more kept crying out, Son of David, have mercy on me.

en.L: And many were rebuking him, [telling him] to be silent; but he kept crying out all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
en.B: Many people scolded him and told him to keep quiet, but he kept shouting even more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
en.R: Many people told him off and said, "Be quiet!" But he shouted even louder, "Son of David, show mercy to me!"

es.L: Y muchos lo reprendían para que callara; pero él gritaba mucho más: «¡Hijo de David, ten piedad de mí!».
es.B: Muchos lo regañaban y le decían que se callara, pero él gritaba todavía más: «¡Hijo de David, ten piedad de mí!».
es.R: Mucha gente lo regañó y le dijo: «¡Cállate!». Pero él gritó todavía más fuerte: «¡Hijo de David, ten compasión de mí!».

sw.L: Na wengi walikuwa wakimkemea ili anyamaze; lakini yeye alizidi sana kupaza sauti, "Mwana wa Daudi, nihurumie!"
sw.B: Watu wengi walimkemea na kumwambia anyamaze, lakini yeye aliendelea kupiga kelele zaidi, "Mwana wa Daudi, nihurumie!"
sw.R: Watu wengi walimkaripia, wakamwambia, "Nyamaza!" Lakini yeye akapiga kelele kwa nguvu zaidi, "Mwana wa Daudi, nionee huruma!"

decisions.choice: were rebuking: sternly telling him to stop
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the disciples with the children (10:13).

decisions.choice: kept crying out all the more: an imperfect, he would not stop
decisions.reason: The tense pictures him shouting again and again, louder each time.

decisions.choice: said, "Be quiet!"
decisions.reason: Readable turns the order into the words spoken.

source.text: καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Φωνήσατε αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And having stopped Jesus said, Call him.

en.L: And Jesus stopped and said, "Call him."
en.B: Jesus stood still and said, "Call him over."
en.R: Jesus stopped walking. He said, "Tell him to come here."

es.L: Y Jesús, deteniéndose, dijo: «{{plural_you:Llámenlo|Llamadlo}}».
es.B: Jesús se detuvo y dijo: «{{plural_you:Llámenlo|Llamadlo}}».
es.R: Jesús dejó de caminar. Dijo: «{{plural_you:Díganle|Decidle}} que venga aquí».

sw.L: Naye Yesu akasimama, akasema, "Mwiteni."
sw.B: Yesu alisimama, akasema, "Mwiteni aje."
sw.R: Yesu aliacha kutembea, akasimama. Akasema, "Mwambieni aje hapa."

decisions.choice: stopped: stood still
decisions.reason: Jesus halts on his way to Jerusalem to answer the cry.

decisions.choice: call: summon
decisions.reason: The verb means to call someone to come. Mark uses it three times in 10:49.

source.text: καὶ φωνοῦσι τὸν τυφλὸν λέγοντες αὐτῷ· Θάρσει, ἔγειρε, φωνεῖ σε.

records.literal_gloss: And they call the blind man saying to him, Take courage, rise up, he calls you.

en.L: And they call the blind man, saying to him, "Take courage, get up; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is calling you."
en.B: So they called to the blind man and told him, "Take courage! Get up! He is calling you."
en.R: So the people called the blind man. They said to him, "It is all right! Get up! Jesus is calling you."

es.L: Y llaman al ciego, diciéndole: «Ánimo, levántate; te llama».
es.B: Entonces llamaron al ciego y le dijeron: «¡Ánimo! ¡Levántate! Te está llamando».
es.R: Entonces la gente llamó al ciego. Le dijeron: «¡Tranquilo! ¡Levántate! Jesús te está llamando».

sw.L: Nao wanamwita yule kipofu, wakimwambia, "Jipe moyo, inuka; anakuita."
sw.B: Basi walimwita yule kipofu, wakamwambia, "Jipe moyo! Inuka! Anakuita."
sw.R: Basi watu walimwita yule kipofu. Wakamwambia, "Usiogope! Inuka! Yesu anakuita."

decisions.choice: take courage: do not be afraid, be cheerful
decisions.reason: Jesus says the same word to the disciples on the lake (6:50).

decisions.choice: they call: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: they call, he calls: the crowd that silenced him now summons him
decisions.reason: The repeated verb shows the change in the crowd and Jesus' call to the man.

decisions.choice: Jesus is calling you
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποβαλὼν τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ ἀναπηδήσας ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: And having cast away the cloak of him, having jumped up he came to Jesus.

en.L: And throwing off his cloak, he jumped up [and] came to Jesus.
en.B: He threw off his cloak, sprang to his feet and came to Jesus.
en.R: Bartimaeus threw his coat to one side, jumped up and went to Jesus.

es.L: Y él, arrojando su manto, se levantó de un salto [y] fue hacia Jesús.
es.B: Él arrojó su manto, se puso en pie de un salto y fue hacia Jesús.
es.R: Bartimeo tiró a un lado su capa, se levantó de un salto y fue hacia Jesús.

sw.L: Naye, akilitupa vazi lake, aliruka juu, akaja kwa Yesu.
sw.B: Alilitupa kando vazi lake la nje, akaruka, akasimama, akamwendea Yesu.
sw.R: Bartimayo alitupa koti lake kando, akaruka juu, akamwendea Yesu.

decisions.choice: cloak: the outer garment, a poor man's covering by day and night
decisions.reason: A beggar might spread his cloak to collect coins, and it was his blanket at night (Exodus 22:26-27). He leaves it behind in his eagerness.

decisions.choice: jumped up: leapt to his feet
decisions.reason: The verb shows his eagerness.

decisions.choice: coat
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for the outer garment.

decisions.choice: vazi (L); vazi lake la nje (B); koti (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the outer garment, a poor man's covering by day and night (meaning decision m1). Balanced says "outer garment" so it is not taken for any piece of clothing; Readable uses "koti", as the English Readable says "coat".

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Τί σοι θέλεις ποιήσω;

records.literal_gloss: And answering him Jesus said, What for you do you desire I should do?

en.L: And Jesus answered him and said, "What do you want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"
en.B: Jesus said to him in reply, "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"
en.R: Jesus asked him, "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

es.L: Y respondiéndole, Jesús dijo: «¿Qué quieres que te haga?».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «¿Qué quieres que haga por ti?».
es.R: Jesús le preguntó: «¿Qué quieres que haga por ti?».

sw.L: Naye Yesu akamjibu, akasema, "Unataka {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nikufanyie nini?"
sw.B: Yesu alimjibu, "Ungependa nikufanyie nini?"
sw.R: Yesu alimwuliza, "Ungependa nikufanyie nini?"

decisions.choice: what do you want me to do for you: the same question as in 10:36
decisions.reason: Jesus asked James and John the same thing. They asked for glory; this man asks for sight.

decisions.choice: answering: speaking in response to the man's cry
decisions.reason: Jesus responds to the man's coming.

source.text: ὁ δὲ τυφλὸς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ραββουνι, ἵνα ἀναβλέψω.

records.literal_gloss: And the blind man said to him, Rabbouni, that I may see again.

en.L: And the blind man said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbouni, [I want] to see again."
en.B: The blind man said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbouni, I want to see again."
en.R: The blind man answered, "My Teacher, I want to be able to see again."

es.L: Y el ciego {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Rabuni, [quiero] volver a ver».
es.B: El ciego {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondió: «Rabuni, quiero volver a ver».
es.R: El ciego respondió: «Maestro mío, quiero volver a ver».

sw.L: Na yule kipofu akamwambia, "Rabuni, [nataka] nione tena."
sw.B: Yule kipofu alimwambia, "Rabuni, nataka kuona tena."
sw.R: Yule kipofu alijibu, "Mwalimu wangu, nataka kuweza kuona tena."

decisions.choice: Rabbouni: an Aramaic form of Rabbi, my master, my teacher
decisions.reason: The word is a fuller, more personal form of Rabbi. Mary Magdalene uses it of the risen Jesus in John 20:16.

decisions.choice: see again: regain sight, or look up
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to see again, as if he had once been able to see. It can also mean simply to look up or to gain sight.

decisions.choice: that I may see: a request with the main verb left out
decisions.reason: The words mean "I want to see" or "let me see".

decisions.choice: My Teacher
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title means, as it says "Teacher" for Rabbi.

decisions.choice: Rabuni (L, B); Maestro mío (R)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic title, "my master, my teacher" (meaning decision m1), spelled as in John 20:16. Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Rabuni (L, B); Mwalimu wangu (R)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic title, "my master, my teacher" (meaning decision m1), spelled as in John 20:16. Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὕπαγε, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus said to him, Go, the faith of you has saved you.

en.L: And Jesus said to him, "Go; your faith has saved you."
en.B: Jesus told him, "Go. Your faith has saved you and made you well."
en.R: Jesus said to him, "Go. Your faith has made you well and saved you."

es.L: Y Jesús le dijo: «Ve, tu fe te ha salvado».
es.B: Jesús le dijo: «Vete. Tu fe te ha salvado y te ha sanado».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «Vete. Tu fe te ha sanado y te ha salvado».

sw.L: Naye Yesu akamwambia, "Nenda; imani yako imekuokoa."
sw.B: Yesu alimwambia, "Nenda. Imani yako imekuokoa na kukuponya."
sw.R: Yesu alimwambia, "Nenda. Imani yako imekuponya na kukuokoa."

decisions.choice: has saved: has made well, and more
decisions.reason: The verb means both healing and rescue by God, as in 5:34. The man's sight is restored, and he follows Jesus on the way.

decisions.choice: faith: trust in Jesus to help him
decisions.reason: His faith was shown in his crying out and coming to Jesus. Jesus credits his faith, as he did the woman's in 5:34.

decisions.choice: go: you are free to go
decisions.reason: Jesus sends him on his way healed. He chooses to follow Jesus instead.

decisions.choice: saved you and made you well (B); made you well and saved you (R)
decisions.reason: As at 5:34, Balanced and Readable give both senses of the verb: the healing and the saving.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνέβλεψεν, καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately he received sight and he was following him on the road.

en.L: And immediately he saw again, and he was following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the way.
en.B: At once his sight came back, and he followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} along the road.
en.R: Right away the man could see again. He went with Jesus along the road and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y al instante recobró la vista, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguía en el camino.
es.B: Al momento recobró la vista y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió por el camino.
es.R: En seguida el hombre pudo ver otra vez. Fue con Jesús por el camino y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió.

sw.L: Na mara akapata kuona tena, akawa akimfuata njiani.
sw.B: Mara moja aliweza kuona tena, akamfuata njiani.
sw.R: Mara hiyo yule mtu aliweza kuona tena. Akaenda pamoja na Yesu njiani, akamfuata.

decisions.choice: following him on the way: he becomes a disciple on the road to Jerusalem
alternatives: he walked behind for a while
decisions.reason: "Follow" is Mark's word for discipleship (1:18; 8:34), and "the way" is the road to Jerusalem and the cross (10:32). The healed man goes where Jesus goes.

decisions.choice: he saw again: a sight that the disciples still lack
decisions.reason: As with the blind man of 8:22-26, the healing closes a section in which the disciples fail to see what Jesus is teaching about his death.

decisions.choice: was following: an imperfect, he went on following
decisions.reason: The tense shows a continuing action.

decisions.choice: on the way (L); along the road (B, R)
alternatives: on the way at every level
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word that can also mean the way of discipleship. Balanced and Readable describe the road.
